Ms Harlow · hiring manager
Thanks for coming in today. Could you tell me what a typical day looks like when you work with carriers abroad?
You · written
Good morning. I work as logistics coordinator in Brno since three years. In the morning I check all trucks on the road and I write to carriers from Germany and Poland to confirm the loading time. Then I solve problems with delays, for example when the driver is late on the border. In the afternoon I make the plan for the next day and I send documents to the customers.
Ms Harlow · hiring manager
Thank you, that is very clear. Can you tell me about one time a delivery went wrong?
You · written
Yes, last winter we had a truck with medicine products from Germany and the driver had accident on the highway. The truck was stuck for six hours and the customer in Prague was very nervous. I called our other carrier, I found a new truck in two hours and we moved the goods there. The delivery came only four hours late and the customer did not cancel the contract.
Ms Harlow · hiring manager
Thank you, that is a clear example, and arriving only four hours late is a good result. While you arranged the new truck, what did you tell the customer in Prague?
You · written
I called the customer in Prague immediately and I told him the truth, that the driver had accident and the truck is stuck. I said we are looking for a new truck and I promised to send him the new arrival time every hour. He was not happy but he appreciated that I was honest and I kept him informed.
Ms Harlow · hiring manager
Hourly updates sound reassuring, even though she was unhappy at first. Why did you decide that being honest was the best approach?
You · written
I decided this because in logistics the customer must trust us. If I say a lie, he will find the truth later and he will not trust me again. When I am honest, he can plan his own work, for example he can inform his warehouse in Prague. Also it is easier for me, because I do not need to explain many times.
Ms Harlow · hiring manager
So honesty helps him plan, even when the news is bad. When several trucks run late, how do you keep them on track?
You · written
When several trucks are late, first I make a list which delivery is the most urgent, for example medicine or the customer with strict time window. Then I call every driver and I ask the new arrival time. I write all in one table and I inform the customers every hour. If one truck have a big problem, I look for another carrier immediately.
